01 · Context

Half a billion people. One support doorway.

Jio Care chat is the first touchpoint for millions seeking help. At this scale, every unnecessary question in the flow is repeated millions of times.

02 · The problem

The bot is always on, but users still feel stuck.

What it does well
Covers a wide range of issues
Uses intent-based automation
Is always available
Where it fails the user
Repetitive questioning
No sense of progress
No explanation of system actions
Conversation feels circular
User feels blamed for wrong inputs
Core insight
Uncertainty, not automation, is the real source of frustration.
03 · Process

Double Diamond: diverge, converge, twice.

The first diamond found the right problem. The second found the right shape for the answer.

01Problem phase
Empathize
Secondary research across Jio, Airtel and Vi chatbots, conversational UX patterns, and service-design literature on trust and transparency.
02Problem phase
Reframe
Three stakeholder lenses (user, developer, head of customer service) turned into How Might We questions.
03Solution phase
Ideate
Controlled disruption: reverse ideation, brand swaps, form swaps and AI-generated provocations.
04Solution phase
Prototype
Information architecture, wireframes and a clickable Figma prototype built on four design rules.
04 · Reframe

From a better chatbot to a calmer support system.

User lens · Emotional
How might we reduce user anxiety during automated support interactions?
Customer-service lens · Flow
How might we combine automated responses with smooth flow and clear solutions, without repetitive redirections?
Developer lens · System
How might we interpret open-ended queries, handle uncertain cases gracefully, and hand over smoothly when automation can't continue?
"Users don't want to explain their problem repeatedly. They want the system to remember and move forward."
"Conversation without structure feels like delay, not help."

06 · Ideate

What if support didn't look like chat at all?

Reverse ideation
What if care felt procedural instead of conversational? Flipping the premise surfaced structure as the missing ingredient.
Brand swap · Logistics
Borrowed from order tracking: clear stages, predictable timelines and action confirmations.
Brand swap · Banking
Borrowed from mobile banking: formal language, structured forms and confirmation screens that build trust.
Form swap
Conversational steps replaced with toggle cards, pre-filled inputs, one-tap confirmations and Yes/No chips.
Most chatbots ask
How human should the bot sound?
This project asks
How clearly can the system show what it's doing?
07 · Solution

The Intent Trail.

Invisible backend logic becomes a visible, step-by-step journey. Users stop guessing and start understanding.

Issue detected

Action in progress

Resolved or escalated

Saved to history

Wireframes focus on three things: reducing cognitive load, making progress visible, and minimizing user effort.
08 · Design principles

Four rules the system never breaks.

1
Never hide system activity
If the system is processing, the user must see it.
Status for every actionNo silent waiting statesEvery delay explained
2
Replace explanation with confirmation
Users should not explain what the system already knows.
Auto-detect issuesAsk to confirm, not describeSelections over text input
3
Reduce effort at every step
Each interaction must need less effort than the one before.
Pre-filled dataContext-aware responsesNo repeated confirmations
4
The system must remember
Users should never repeat what they've already shared.
Persistent issue historyContext-aware responsesResume interrupted journeys
09 · Designed interfaces

Eight screens, four rules, one calm system.

Each pair of screens below puts one design rule into practice. Read them as a journey: find the issue, confirm it, watch it move, and come back without starting over.

1
Never hide system activity
Issues have a visible state, always.
SCREEN 01
Issue status hub
Right inside the chat, every issue is sorted into Open, In Progress, Resolved or Archived. Users see where things stand before they ask, which removes the "is anyone working on this?" anxiety.
SCREEN 02
Issue inbox
An email-style inbox of support tickets, each labelled with its live state, like "Recharge ₹239 – Pending Activation". Search, filter, refresh, archive and history sit in one toolbar; New Issue is always one tap away.
2
Replace explanation with confirmation
Select and confirm instead of typing and describing.
SCREEN 03
Guided welcome
The conversation opens with large, tappable categories (recharges, plans, 5G, network, SIM, JioFiber, language) instead of an empty text box. Intent is captured in one tap, so the bot never has to guess.
SCREEN 04
Auto-detected context
The user taps "Recharge Wrong Plan" and the bot already knows about the recent recharge. No number, amount or date is requested; it points straight to the open issue where the fix lives.
3
Reduce user effort at every step
The system shows its work, so the user doesn't have to chase it.
SCREEN 05 · KEY SCREEN
The Intent Trail
A timestamped log of what the system did: draft created, compatibility warning shown, intent confirmed, payment successful, activation scheduled with undo available. Backend logic becomes a story the user can read in seconds.
SCREEN 06
Issue detail with one clear action
Status, plan, number and an activation countdown are pre-filled. Because no usage is detected yet, a single action is offered (Cancel & Change Plan) and its consequence is stated before the tap: the amount is adjusted, not refunded.
4
The system must remember
Nothing shared once is ever asked for again.
SCREEN 07
Pay only the difference
When switching to the right plan, the system remembers the ₹239 already paid and asks only for ₹110. Payment method is a single choice, with Pay Now and Go Back as clear exits.
SCREEN 08
Resume where you left off
Returning users find the earlier conversation and quick options intact. An interrupted journey picks up from the last step instead of restarting from "How can I help you?".
10 · Scenario 2

Wrong recharge, fixed with the difference.

Instead of a refund dispute over chat, the system recognises what was already paid and asks only for the balance on the plan the user meant to buy.

11 · User flows

Every failure lands somewhere safe.

Old chat flows end in a loop: the user explains, the bot asks again, the conversation restarts. The redesigned flows route every outcome through a preserved state with clear exits.
